accepted.s: In Jain philosophy, which one of the following correctly describes Jiva and Ajiva?
o: Jiva is consciousness and Ajiva is non-conscious matter
Jiva is matter and Ajiva is consciousness
Jiva denotes ritual and Ajiva denotes liberation
Both Jiva and Ajiva denote material bondage
accepted.x: Jiva refers to the conscious soul, whereas Ajiva denotes non-conscious matter or non-living reality.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related paired terms by their defining meanings.
accepted.sec: Jain concepts and practices - jiva/ajiva, karma, kaivalya, sallekhana

accepted.s: Which one of the following best explains the Jain conception of Karma?
o: A divine reward granted by the creator
A material bondage of the soul causing rebirth
A form of meditation leading directly to Siddha status
accepted.x: In Jainism, karma is understood as material bondage clinging to the soul and causing rebirth.
accepted.tq: Use the exact doctrinal definition rather than a broadly familiar religious meaning.
accepted.sec: Jain concepts and practices - jiva/ajiva, karma, kaivalya, sallekhana

accepted.s: The term ‘Kevala Jnana’ or ‘Kaivalya’ in Jainism refers to:
o: The omniscience attained by the soul
The complete renunciation of worldly life
The ritual fast undertaken at the end of life
accepted.x: Kevala Jnana or Kaivalya is the state of omniscience attained by the soul after the removal of karmic bondage.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise technical meaning of a philosophical term.
accepted.sec: Jain concepts and practices - jiva/ajiva, karma, kaivalya, sallekhana

accepted.s: A soul that has become fully liberated is known in Jainism as a:
accepted.x: A Siddha is a fully liberated soul. Jina and Nirgrantha are titles or designations associated with Jainism, while a Ganadhara is a chief disciple.
accepted.tq: Separate related Jain designations by their exact status or function.
accepted.sec: Jain concepts and practices - jiva/ajiva, karma, kaivalya, sallekhana

accepted.s: Sallekhana or Santhara is associated with which of the following practices?
o: Ritual fasting unto death at the end of life to purify karma
A festival of forgiveness celebrated at the beginning of the year
A ritual of animal sacrifice for attaining liberation
A posture used for meditation by Tirthankaras
accepted.x: Sallekhana, also called Santhara, is the Jain practice of undertaking a ritual fast unto death at the end of life for purification of karma.
accepted.tq: Test the exact association of a distinctive religious practice.
accepted.sec: Jain concepts and practices - jiva/ajiva, karma, kaivalya, sallekhana

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Jainism:
1. Jainism holds that souls may exist in natural objects.
2. The Jain emphasis on extreme ahimsa is connected with the belief that living beings can experience pain.
3. Jainism accepts the authority of the Vedas as the ultimate religious authority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Jainism rejects Vedic authority and is non-theistic.
accepted.tq: Find the one statement that reverses Jainism’s position on Vedic authority.
accepted.sec: Jain concepts and practices - jiva/ajiva, karma, kaivalya, sallekhana

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the Jain view of the origin and functioning of the world?
o: The world runs according to an eternal law of decay and development and has no creator god.
The world is governed by the Vedic sacrificial order.
The world is periodically created by the Tirthankaras.
The world was created and is continuously controlled by a personal creator god.
accepted.x: Jainism is non-theistic and holds that the world functions according to an eternal law of decay and development rather than the will of a creator god.
accepted.tq: Apply the doctrine by identifying the correct position on the creator question.
accepted.sec: Jain concepts and practices - jiva/ajiva, karma, kaivalya, sallekhana

accepted.s: In Jainism, liberation is achieved through which of the following processes?
o: Performing Vedic sacrifices and worshipping a creator deity
Accumulating material possessions and fulfilling worldly desires
Stopping the inflow of karma and shedding accumulated karma through penance
Following fate without undertaking spiritual discipline
accepted.x: Jain liberation involves stopping the inflow of karma and shedding accumulated karma, or nirjara, through penance, ultimately leading to Kevala Jnana and the Siddha state.
accepted.tq: Use the cause-and-effect chain from karmic bondage to liberation.
accepted.sec: Jain concepts and practices - jiva/ajiva, karma, kaivalya, sallekhana

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the four forms of existence recognised in Jainism?
accepted.x: Deva, Manushya, Naraki and Tiryancha are the four forms of existence. Yaksha is not included in this classification.
accepted.tq: Find the outsider in a classification by checking every item against the listed fourfold scheme.
accepted.sec: Jain concepts and practices - jiva/ajiva, karma, kaivalya, sallekhana

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Practice)
a. Paryushana
b. Samvatsari
c. Pratikramana
d. Sallekhana

List-II (Association)
i. Introspection
 ii. Ritual fast unto death
 iii. Jain festival
 iv. Day of forgiveness

Which of the following is the correct combination?
accepted.x: Paryushana is the Jain festival, its last day Samvatsari is the day of forgiveness, Pratikramana is introspection, and Sallekhana is the ritual fast unto death.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and complete the one-to-one matching.
accepted.sec: Jain concepts and practices - jiva/ajiva, karma, kaivalya, sallekhana

accepted.s: The images of Tirthankaras are traditionally shown in which of the following postures?
accepted.x: Jina images are commonly represented in Padmasana or in the standing Kayotsarga posture.
accepted.tq: Distinguish Jain image postures from Buddhist hand gestures and other sculptural forms.
accepted.sec: Jain concepts and practices - jiva/ajiva, karma, kaivalya, sallekhana

accepted.s: Jains were also known by which of the following names?
accepted.x: Jains were called Nigranthas, meaning free from fetters, and Shramanas, referring to ascetic practitioners.
accepted.tq: Recall alternative historical names and avoid substitution with names of other religious groups.
accepted.sec: Jain concepts and practices - jiva/ajiva, karma, kaivalya, sallekhana

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Anekantavada is the doctrine that reality has many sides or facets. Syadvada concerns conditioned predication, Nayavada concerns partial standpoints, and Sallekhana is ritual fasting unto death.
accepted.tq: Separate similar Jain doctrines by matching each term with its precise meaning.
accepted.sec: Jain concepts and practices - jiva/ajiva, karma, kaivalya, sallekhana

accepted.s: Syadvada is best described as:
o: The practice of avoiding all forms of agriculture
The doctrine of material bondage causing rebirth
The theory that only one absolute standpoint is valid
The theory of conditioned predication and relativity of truth
accepted.x: Syadvada is the Jain theory of conditioned predication, expressed through the idea of ‘may be’, and is associated with the seven-fold predication or saptabhangi.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive keyword ‘may be’ to identify conditioned predication.
accepted.sec: Jain concepts and practices - jiva/ajiva, karma, kaivalya, sallekhana

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a vow prescribed among the five anuvratas for Jain householders?
accepted.x: The five vows are non-injury, non-stealing, non-adultery, truth and non-possession. Animal sacrifice is contrary to Jain ahimsa and is not one of the vows.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that conflicts with the central Jain principle of ahimsa.
accepted.sec: Jain concepts and practices - jiva/ajiva, karma, kaivalya, sallekhana

accepted.s: Which one of the following best explains why strict Jain followers traditionally avoided agriculture?
o: Agriculture was considered a form of royal taxation.
Agricultural activity could injure living organisms in the soil.
Jains believed that crops could not be cultivated in India.
Agriculture was reserved exclusively for Buddhist monks.
accepted.x: Because Jain ahimsa extends to all forms of life, strict followers avoided agriculture since ploughing and related activities could injure organisms in the soil. This contributed to a trading base among Jains.
accepted.tq: Apply the principle of extreme ahimsa to an occupational practice.
accepted.sec: Jain concepts and practices - jiva/ajiva, karma, kaivalya, sallekhana

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Religion)
a. Jainism
b. Buddhism
c. Ajivika
d. Saivism

List-II (Founder or key text/principle)
i. Makkhali Gosala
 ii. Mahavira and Agamas
 iii. Gautama Buddha and Tripitaka
 iv. Linga

Which of the following is the correct combination?
accepted.x: Jainism is associated with Mahavira and the Agamas, Buddhism with Gautama Buddha and the Tripitaka, Ajivika with Makkhali Gosala, and Saivism with the Linga.
accepted.tq: Begin with the distinctive founder-text pairs and eliminate inconsistent combinations.
accepted.sec: Religion → founder, text, symbol matching

accepted.s:
Match the following religions with their associated symbol or principle:

List-I
 a. Jainism
 b. Buddhism
 c. Ajivika
 d. Animism

List-II
 i. Nature worship
 ii. Niyati
 iii. Triratna
 iv. Dharmachakra

Which of the following is the correct combination?
accepted.x: Jainism is associated with Triratna, Buddhism with Dharmachakra, Ajivika with Niyati or fate, and Animism with nature worship.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive symbol or principle to establish the correct pairs.
accepted.sec: Religion → founder, text, symbol matching

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Jain hand symbol is correct?
o: It is associated with ahimsa and is shown with a wheel.
It represents the Ajivika doctrine of Niyati.
It represents the Buddhist Eightfold Path.
accepted.x: The Jain hand with a wheel is associated with the principle of ahimsa or non-violence.
accepted.tq: Identify a religious symbol by linking it with its associated principle.
accepted.sec: Religion → founder, text, symbol matching

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Mahavira:
1. He belonged to the Jnatrika clan.
2. His father was Siddhartha.
3. He was born at Kundagrama near Vaishali.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Mahavira was born at Kundagrama near Vaishali, was the son of Siddhartha, and belonged to the Jnatrika clan.
accepted.tq: Combine birthplace, parentage and clan in a compact statement set.
accepted.sec: Mahavira - birth, parents, clan, enlightenment, death, titles

accepted.s: Mahavira’s mother Trishala was the sister of:
o: Makkhali Gosala, the founder of the Ajivikas
Siddhartha, the chief of the Jnatrikas
Chetaka, the chief of the Lichchhavis
accepted.x: Trishala, the mother of Mahavira, was the sister of Chetaka, the chief of the Lichchhavi republic.
accepted.tq: Test a precise kinship relationship using nearby historical personalities as distractors.
accepted.sec: Mahavira - birth, parents, clan, enlightenment, death, titles

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs relating to Mahavira’s family is correctly matched?
o: Wife — Yashoda; daughter — Anojja or Priyadarshana
accepted.x: Mahavira’s wife was Yashoda and his daughter was known as Anojja or Priyadarshana, according to the Svetambara tradition.
accepted.tq: Check the relationship direction carefully in a family-based matching question.
accepted.sec: Mahavira - birth, parents, clan, enlightenment, death, titles

accepted.s: At what age did Mahavira renounce worldly life?
accepted.x: Mahavira renounced worldly life at the age of 30 and subsequently undertook twelve years of rigorous asceticism.
accepted.tq: Use the exact age associated with renunciation and distinguish it from the age of enlightenment.
accepted.sec: Mahavira - birth, parents, clan, enlightenment, death, titles

accepted.s: Mahavira practised rigorous asceticism for approximately:
accepted.x: Mahavira underwent twelve years of severe asceticism before attaining Kevala Jnana.
accepted.tq: Separate the duration of asceticism from the duration of companionship with Gosala.
accepted.sec: Mahavira - birth, parents, clan, enlightenment, death, titles

accepted.s: Mahavira attained Kevala Jnana at:
o: Jrimbhikagrama on the bank of the Rijupalika, under a sal tree
Pavapuri on the bank of the Ganga
Rajagriha on the bank of the Son
accepted.x: Mahavira attained Kevala Jnana at Jrimbhikagrama, on the bank of the Rijupalika river, under a sal tree.
accepted.tq: Combine place, river and tree to identify the exact enlightenment site.
accepted.sec: Mahavira - birth, parents, clan, enlightenment, death, titles

accepted.s: According to the traditional account, Mahavira attained Kevala Jnana at the age of:
accepted.x: Mahavira attained Kevala Jnana at the age of 42, after twelve years of rigorous asceticism.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the age of enlightenment from the ages of renunciation and death.
accepted.sec: Mahavira - birth, parents, clan, enlightenment, death, titles

accepted.s: Mahavira breathed his last at Pavapuri near Rajagriha at the age of:
accepted.x: Mahavira died at Pavapuri near Rajagriha at the age of 72. The traditional date associated with his death is 527 BCE.
accepted.tq: Link the death place with the correct age and avoid confusing it with the age of enlightenment.
accepted.sec: Mahavira - birth, parents, clan, enlightenment, death, titles

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a title associated with Mahavira?
accepted.x: Jina, Kevalin, Nirgrantha, Mahavira and Arhat are titles associated with Mahavira. Tathagata is a title associated with the Buddha.
accepted.tq: Find the title belonging to another religious tradition rather than Jainism.
accepted.sec: Mahavira - birth, parents, clan, enlightenment, death, titles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Mahavira’s disciples is correct?
o: He had eleven Ganadharas, and Arya Sudharma survived him and became the first Thera.
Chetaka was appointed as the chief Ganadhara.
Makkhali Gosala became the first Thera after Mahavira’s death.
He had five Ganadharas, all of whom survived him.
accepted.x: Mahavira had eleven chief disciples or Ganadharas. Arya Sudharma was the only one to survive him and became the first Thera.
accepted.tq: Use membership and succession details to reject swapped-person statements.
accepted.sec: Mahavira - birth, parents, clan, enlightenment, death, titles

accepted.s: Makkhali Gosala was associated with Mahavira as his companion for approximately:
accepted.x: Makkhali Gosala was Mahavira’s companion for about six years before founding the Ajivika sect. Jain accounts generally describe him as a companion or disciple rather than as Mahavira’s guru.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a precise duration from the longer period of Mahavira’s asceticism.
accepted.sec: Mahavira - birth, parents, clan, enlightenment, death, titles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the relationship between Mahavira and Makkhali Gosala is correct?
o: Gosala accompanied Mahavira for some years before founding the Ajivika sect.
Gosala founded the Jain Sangha after Mahavira’s death.
Gosala became the only surviving Ganadhara of Mahavira.
Gosala was Mahavira’s father and chief patron.
accepted.x: Makkhali Gosala was Mahavira’s companion for some years and later founded the Ajivika sect. Jain texts do not generally treat him as Mahavira’s guru.
accepted.tq: Avoid the swapped-role trap involving a closely associated religious personality.
accepted.sec: Mahavira - birth, parents, clan, enlightenment, death, titles

accepted.s: Which republic is described as the first to recognise Jainism?
accepted.x: The Lichchhavi republic is identified as the first republic to recognise Jainism.
accepted.tq: Recall the specific political community associated with early recognition of Jainism.
accepted.sec: Mahavira - birth, parents, clan, enlightenment, death, titles

accepted.s: Chandragupta Maurya is traditionally associated with which Jain practice at Shravanabelagola?
accepted.x: Chandragupta Maurya is traditionally said to have performed Sallekhana at Shravanabelagola.
accepted.tq: Match a historical personality with the distinctive practice associated with him.
accepted.sec: Jain concepts and practices - jiva/ajiva, karma, kaivalya, sallekhana
